entries.title: Standard order: one customer, one line, in stock
entries.question: Is it committed, reserved, shipped, invoiced, paid?
entries.summary: Reality derives the customer invoice's open amount from its posted receivable and the payments or credits allocated to it. The invoice is fully settled when the derived open amount reaches zero; an allocation that covers only part leaves the remainder open.

localized_summaries.de: Reality leitet den offenen Betrag einer Kundenrechnung aus der gebuchten Forderung und den zugeordneten Zahlungen oder Gutschriften ab. Die Rechnung ist vollständig ausgeglichen, sobald der offene Betrag null erreicht; eine Teilzahlung lässt den Rest offen.

limitations: A person names the second warehouse; Reality does not spread a reservation across warehouses by itself.
Proven with twelve lines; the rule does not depend on the number of lines.

entries.title: Stock exists but is blocked (quality, quarantine, expiry)
entries.question: Is blocked stock excluded from availability?
entries.summary: Reality evaluates: Is blocked stock excluded from availability? Stock is blocked where it lies with a reason (quality, damage, expiry, inspection), optionally by lot or pallet; it stays physically there and is excluded from availability, reservation, shipping and transfer until it is released or scrapped through the review.
limitations: Nothing blocks by itself: an expired lot is reported and blocked by a person.
Quality management workflows beyond block, release and scrap are not modelled.

entries.title: Stock exists in the wrong warehouse
entries.question: Is a transfer needed, and is availability per location?
entries.summary: Reality evaluates: Is a transfer needed, and is availability per location? When an order's warehouse cannot cover a line but another warehouse can, Stock in another warehouse names where the stock is and what it could cover, and offers to reserve it there or to transfer it to the order's warehouse, both through the review.
limitations: The finding allocates nothing; two orders may be shown the same stock until one reserves it.
Stock in transit between warehouses is not modelled; a transfer moves stock at once.

entries.title: Stock only on order (open purchase)
entries.question: Can it be promised (available to promise)?
entries.summary: Reality evaluates: Can it be promised (available to promise)? Available to promise answers per item what is free now and, per open purchase in the order of its stated date, how much more becomes free, naming the purchase, its supplier and whether it is overdue; what a purchase's customer assignments still expect is not offered again.
limitations: Purchase dates are what the supplier stated; an overdue purchase still counts and is marked overdue.
The answer is company-wide over stock locations, not per warehouse.

entries.title: Receipt resolves backorders
entries.question: Which commitment is served first?
entries.summary: Reality evaluates: Which commitment is served first? After a receipt, Serve backorders proposes reservations in a stated order: the orders the received purchase is assigned to, in assignment order, then the others by due date. A person may change the quantities and confirms; nothing is reserved by the receipt itself.
limitations: There is no priority per customer; a person states a different split by changing the quantities.
Lot- and serial-tracked items are reserved lot by lot, not through Serve backorders.

entries.title: Receipt covers only part of the backorders
entries.question: Which remain uncovered?
entries.summary: Reality evaluates: Which remain uncovered? Supply coverage splits each assignment into what has arrived and what is still to come, in the order the assignments were made; Serve backorders reserves what arrived in that order, and the promises left short stay at risk.
limitations: The split is a read-time observation; once a person reserves, the reservation decides.

entries.title: Customer refuses partial delivery
entries.question: Reserved but deliberately not shipped — why?
entries.summary: Reality evaluates: Reserved but deliberately not shipped — why? A customer, or one order, states ship complete with a reason: readiness names the rule while any open line cannot ship in full, a partial shipment is refused with its code, and Order waiting for completeness names the ready and missing lines. A person can lift the rule for one order with a reason through the review.
limitations: Complete means the whole order; there is no per-line or parcel-count rule (B11).
An importer recording what a source says left is not refused.

entries.title: Credit limit exceeded: order held, released by a person

entries.summary: Reality evaluates: Who released it, and why? An invoice recorded without links to its order lines counts next to the order until the order is closed.

entries.title: Picking error caught before shipment
entries.question: Corrected without a false movement?
entries.summary: Reality evaluates: Corrected without a false movement? Picking more than planned is refused before anything moves, a wrong pick goes back by a put-back that is a true movement, and the dispatch is refused until what is picked matches the planned delivery.

entries.title: Picking error found by the customer
entries.question: Wrong item shipped, right item still open?
entries.summary: Reality evaluates: Wrong item shipped, right item still open? The recorded shipment is corrected to the item that actually left, naming the order line it was meant for. The line is open again for the right item, stock of both items is true, and Wrong item delivered names the line until the wrong goods come back.
limitations: Reshipping the right item is an ordinary dispatch of the open line.

entries.title: Parcel lost, carrier insurance pays
entries.question: Goods gone, claim receivable, customer still served?
entries.summary: Reality evaluates: Goods gone, claim receivable, customer still served? A lost parcel is recorded as a failed delivery: its shipment no longer counts as delivered, the goods are written off, the promise is open again to ship once more, and a claim against the carrier or its insurer is an open receivable that the carrier's payment settles.
limitations: A failure covers the whole shipment, not one package of several.
The claim amount is stated; it is not derived from the goods' cost.
question_examples: Parcel lost, carrier insurance pays
Goods gone, claim receivable, customer still served?
The carrier lost a parcel; how do we claim it and send the order again?
Der Spediteur hat ein Paket verloren; wie machen wir die Forderung geltend und liefern neu?

entries.title: Parcel undeliverable, returns
entries.question: Stock back, commitment reopened?
entries.summary: Reality evaluates: Stock back, commitment reopened? An undeliverable parcel is recorded as a failed delivery, not a customer return: its shipment no longer counts as delivered, the goods are back where they left from, and the promise is open again; an invoice already issued is reported as invoiced and not shipped until the order ships again.
limitations: The goods come back to the location they left from.
Reshipping or cancelling is a separate decision with the existing tools.
question_examples: Parcel undeliverable, returns
Stock back, commitment reopened?
A parcel came back because the address was wrong; is the order open again?
Ein Paket kam unzustellbar zurück; ist der Auftrag wieder offen?

entries.title: Delivery refused
entries.question: Same as D08 with a reason?
entries.summary: Reality evaluates: Same as D08 with a reason? A refused delivery is a failed delivery with the stated refusal reason, shown on the shipment; the goods are back and the promise is open again to ship once more or cancel.
limitations: The reason is free text.
question_examples: Delivery refused
Same as D08 with a reason?
The customer refused the parcel at the door; how do we record why?

entries.title: Drop shipping: supplier ships directly
entries.question: Customer served without own stock movement?
entries.summary: Reality evaluates: Customer served without own stock movement? Yes. A purchase order that ships to the customer is assigned to the order line; when the supplier states that it shipped, one reviewed drop shipment keeps the purchase and the customer order at once, with a shipment carrying the supplier's carrier and tracking number, and the company's stock does not change.
limitations: The supplier's dispatch is recorded through the reviewed action; supplier portals and dispatch advices are not interpreted.
The contribution read does not cost a drop-shipped line from its purchase price.
Until the supplier's dispatch is recorded, the warehouse queue lists the line as not reserved.
question_examples: Drop shipping: supplier ships directly
Customer served without own stock movement?
The supplier ships straight to our customer; how do we record it?

entries.title: Partial drop shipping: part own stock, part supplier
entries.question: Both paths fulfil one commitment?
entries.summary: Reality evaluates: Both paths fulfil one commitment? Yes. The part in stock is reserved and shipped as usual, the rest is drop-shipped by the supplier against its assigned purchase, and the one customer order is delivered in full by both.
limitations: Which part the supplier ships is stated by the assignment of the drop-ship purchase.

entries.title: 3PL confirms shipments late
entries.question: Is the lag visible and later closed?
entries.summary: Reality evaluates: Is the lag visible and later closed? A shipment confirmed late states when the goods actually moved; its movements carry that time, while the shipment keeps when Reality was told and shows the confirmation lag between them. Overdue and stalled findings raised in the meantime clear as soon as the confirmation is recorded.
limitations: 3PL messages are not interpreted from a source; the confirmation is recorded through the reviewed shipment tool.
A late confirmation is shown, not reported as a finding of its own.

entries.summary: Reality evaluates: Shipment dated to the slot? A planned delivery states its booked slot; the shipment keeps the slot it was booked for, and a slot that closed before anything shipped is shown as missed.

limitations: Only an item in the ordered item's unit can stand in; the line keeps the item it ordered.

An agent can prepare the run; a person confirms it.
limitations: Letters and emails are not sent; the notice is recorded evidence.
The schedule is one per company with a fixed fee per level, charged in each notice's currency; interest is not calculated.
Disputed items are not known to Reality; the person deselects them in the review.

entries.title: Two parties merged as duplicates
entries.question: History of both kept?
entries.summary: Reality evaluates: History of both kept? Yes. A reviewed merge states that one business partner is a duplicate of another, with a reason. Nothing stated is rewritten: each record keeps naming the partner it states, and the survivor's detail, balance and credit exposure include the duplicate's. The duplicate's detail names its survivor. Merged partners are never merged again, so there are no chains.
limitations: A merge is not undone.
The company's own business partner and a partner with an open delivery hold are not merged.

entries.title: Supplier item number ≠ own number, several suppliers
entries.question: Supplier item mapping?
entries.summary: Reality evaluates: Supplier item mapping? Per supplier, a reviewed statement says which of our items the supplier's own number names, with the supplier's name for it; every supplier has its own numbers for the same item. Purchase orders and supplier invoices entered by hand or by chat resolve lines by that number, keep it on the line as stated, and the purchase order, the invoice and the three-way match show it.
limitations: Numbers are matched ignoring case and spaces; there is no fuzzy matching.
An unknown supplier number is refused at entry; documents from a supplier's own system (EDI, order confirmations by file) are not interpreted yet.

entries.title: Customer orders 10, 4 in stock, prepayment 80 % paid, released anyway, 4 shipped; 6 reordered, supplier delivers 5 in two dates; customer cancels 1; rest shipped; 2 returned damaged
entries.question: Every quantity and every euro reconciles at the end.
entries.summary: Reality evaluates: Every quantity and every euro reconciles at the end. An 80 % prepaid order is refused until a company owner releases it with a reason; it ships in two parts while the supplier delivers 5 of 6 on two dates, one unit is cancelled and two come back damaged and are scrapped, and a credit for three settles the open 20 and refunds the 10 paid too much.
limitations: The release covers the order's stated amount and lets the order ship before it is paid; the unpaid rest stays an ordinary open receivable until it is paid or credited.
Raising a line's quantity does not raise the prepayment the order requires, because the gate measures the order's stated gross amount.
question_examples: Customer orders 10, 4 in stock, prepayment 80 % paid, released anyway, 4 shipped; 6 reordered, supplier delivers 5 in two dates; customer cancels 1; rest shipped; 2 returned damaged

entries.question: Cancelled demand leaves the purchase assignment.
entries.summary: Reality evaluates: Cancelled demand leaves the purchase assignment. Two orders assigned to one purchase, the purchase comes short and is reduced, a person reserves the key customer first by stating the quantities, and the other order's cancellation ends its assignment and releases its reservation.
limitations: Which customer is key is the person's decision; there is no stated customer priority.

entries.title: Drop shipment with wrong item; customer returns it to us instead of the supplier
entries.question: Ownership and credits on both sides.
entries.summary: Reality evaluates: Ownership and credits on both sides. A drop-shipped order returned to the company comes into its stock as an ordinary return and is reported until the customer is credited; sent on to the supplier against the drop-ship purchase, it is reported until the supplier credits it, and both sides net out. The wrong item itself cannot be named.
limitations: The drop shipment records the ordered item; naming the different item the supplier actually sent is a separate gap (D05).
question_examples: Drop shipment with wrong item; customer returns it to us instead of the supplier
Ownership and credits on both sides.

entries.question: Every position allocated.
entries.summary: Reality evaluates: Every position allocated. One reviewed settlement books 400 charges against their invoices, 12 refunds against their credit notes, 3 chargebacks as returned payments and the fees, and the provider's account is empty afterwards.
limitations: The settlement reads and writes each line through the shared payment primitives, so its cost grows with the lines; a statement holds at most 2000 lines.

entries.title: Customer is also a supplier, with an overdue receivable, an open credit and a new order above the credit limit
entries.question: Hold reason names all facts.
entries.summary: Reality evaluates: Hold reason names all facts. For a customer who is also a supplier, a new order past the limit is held with a reason that names the overdue receivable, the ordered value, the open credit subtracted and the payable to the same party, which is named but not netted.
limitations: Payables are not netted against receivables; that needs an agreement.
